But this does not match the earlier mapping of 'p_8(x)' in the seventh FOL-NL pair: 'If x either investigates the deep sea or analyzes ocean samples, but not both, then x specializes in marine life.' That is, p_8(x) was defined contextually as a consequence of behavior, not a general specialization implying discoveries. More critically, compare this statement to the ninth FOL-NL pair: 'p_8(Rivka') → (p_7(Rivka') ⊕ p_9(Rivka'))', which says that if she specializes in marine life, then she makes discoveries or authors papers — but not both. That implication (with exclusive or) would contradict the simpler 'p_8 → p_7', which asserts that specializing always leads to discoveries, regardless of paper authorship. Thus, 'p_8 → p_7' contradicts the earlier more nuanced conditional involving an exclusive or. Therefore, the last FOL-NL pair is incorrect because the FOL statement over-simplifies and contradicts a prior consistent logical structure.
